summary: In this excerpt from Book 14, a narrator leaves a party in freezing rain and snow with Ian, Geoff, and the sleeping Zeke, who has been teasing the narrator about the name Zenobia. Ian drives the narrator home in his rental car, and the conversation turns to Zeke's background: a brilliant young man who dropped out of Ian's class, rejects rules and money, travels constantly, and has friends everywhere. The passage closes with Ian noting that being accepted to MIT at fourteen can distort one's social awareness.
one_line: A narrator leaves a snowy party with Ian and Geoff and learns about the brilliant, rule-averse Zeke from Ian.
key_facts: Zeke apologized to the narrator for making fun of the narrator's name and admitted he had pictured a different person named Shad, not a girl named Zenobia.
Zeke said he went by 'Zeke the Freak' within the first two minutes at preschool and hated school.
Outside the party, the freezing rain had turned into snow.
Ian said the narrator could not ride a bike in such awful weather, and the narrator took off the front wheel and stowed the bike in Ian's trunk.
Geoff put the empty pizza boxes and case of empties into his rental car.
Zeke, who had no car, climbed into the back seat of Ian's rental and fell asleep snoring.
Zeke hitched a ride up from Chicago with a truck driver and had no place to stay.
Ian said he had known Zeke since Zeke was twelve.
Zeke took a class from Ian once, when he was younger than the narrator, but dropped out before the semester ended.
Ian described Zeke as brilliant but uninterested in following rules or filling out forms, and as someone who thinks money is stupid.
Ian said Zeke picks up freelance work to make a living and travels constantly with friends everywhere.
Jason and Tyler stayed behind to take apart the traveling Faraday cage and erase all signs of the group's presence.
Ian told the narrator that being accepted to MIT at fourteen can mess up one's grasp of social norms.
The narrator said they were used to riding in snow and not used to letting people tell them what to do.
